title: release-chorus: lifecycle ledger and staged-promotion choreography
author: Marcus Patel
release_notes: Introduce Release Chorus: a unified lifecycle coordinator that consolidates staged promotion, A/B routing, and shadow capture into a single control plane.
Add immutable lifecycle ledger to persist decision traces for deterministic replay and auditability.
Provide a migration script to upgrade existing Rollout resources to the new choreography schema with safe fallback semantics.
Console: new Release timeline view, per-release decision trace, and replay controls for shadow traffic.
CLI: rollout promote/demote primitives and a dry-run mode for the ledger migration.
No customer-facing API change for hosted endpoints — rollout semantics are opt-in via new rollout kind annotations.
description: Motivation: Multiple internal rollout implementations (staged-promote, shadow-bridge, cohort-slicer) had overlapping logic and diverging audit trails which made incident triage and deterministic replays difficult. This PR introduces 'Release Chorus', a compact choreography runtime and an append-only lifecycle ledger that records every routing and decision event so rollouts can be replayed, audited, and rolled back deterministically. Design summary: (1) choreography controller: a lightweight FSM that orchestrates promotion phases, graceful shadow drains, and A/B fraction ramps; (2) lifecycle ledger: single append-only datastore (pluggable backends) that captures inputs, policy decisions, and resulting route deltas; (3) migration shim: transforms existing Rollout resources into the new choreography representation and seeds ledger entries so past promotions remain reproducible; (4) replay harness: a test utility to reapply ledger events against a snapshot to validate rollback paths. Backwards compatibility: existing Rollout CRs remain valid. Migration is performed by the included scripts/migrate-rollout-ledger.sh and is opt-in; if migration is skipped the system will continue to honor the legacy controller. Telemetry and safety: integrated with the Console to expose a per-release timeline and decision trace; added new SLO gates that can be bound to release steps. Risk and mitigation: large change area in control plane and console — rollout staged rollout to internal tenants for two weeks using the smoke-harness, then host-wide enablement. Testing: unit tests for choreography state machine, ledger durability tests (mock backends), and an integration replay test that replays a 10k-event shadow capture trace in CI. Migration: the migration script is idempotent and includes a dry-run flag; a small DB migration is required for the ledger index (migrate-runner applies it automatically). Related work: RFC-2026 (release choreography) and ENG-2345 track implementation. Checklist: 1) implementation and unit tests complete, 2) migration script + dry-run, 3) console and CLI UX connected, 4) integration replay tests added, 5) phased rollout plan documented in docs/release-chorus-rollout-plan.md.

review_comments: Sofia Morales: Please add a short description of how the ledger handles clock skew and eventual consistency across control plane replicas.

Marcus Patel: Reply: ledger writes are designed to be idempotent by event ID and we added a vector-timestamp envelope; documentation updated in docs/release-chorus-rollout-plan.md to explain skew handling.
Ethan Li: Could the migration lock the Rollout objects during seed to avoid double-promote? Consider a per-namespace semaphore.
Marcus Patel: Reply: implemented per-namespace migration leases in scripts/migrate-rollout-ledger.sh and added safety checks — see migration guide.
Priya Nair: Tests look good; please add a metrics tag to differentiate replay-origin events from live events so SLO dashboards can filter them.
Marcus Patel: Reply: added event.origin tag and updated the metrics doc. Ready for final review.
Sofia Morales: Approved after small nits were addressed.
